text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A delegation of some 50 representatives of Germany's biggest firms will be on a two-day visit to Belgrade.
- Claims that the exchange rate is unrealistic and non-stimulating exports are untrue, says vice-governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia Ratko Banovic.
- Rehabiliation of the agrarian sector is necessary, says Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Nedeljko Sipovac.
- Central Serbia and Vojvodina will lose ont third of their population by the year 2050, according to experts of the faculty of economics.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno starts election campaign with rallies in Pozarevac and Jagodina.
- Kosovo Albanian leader Ibrahim Rugova says it is important that the resolution of the Kosovo issue is a condition for lifting of the so-called outer-wall of sanctions against Yugoslavia.
- Domestic textile and leather industry mostly processing goods supplied by foreign partners due to lack of raw materials and funds to purchase them.
- Macedonian defence minister Blagoje Handziski arriving in Yugoslavia today amid speculation that Yugoslavia will sell surplus arms under the Dayton agreement to Macedonia.
- IMF's fourth condition for Yugoslavia's return has been met with the final lifting of the sanctons says, head of the Yugoslav negotiating team with the fund Oskar Kovac.
- Consumer basket of basic food products for a four member family stood at 1,409 dinars in September, which is 2.6 percent higher than in August.
- Regulation banning sales of all but second-hand goods at flea markets enters into effect today.
